subject: Renewal — Centrica: soft cap proposal, banded discount and commit uplift
raw:
From: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev@centrica.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Kim <leah.kim@centrica.io>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning for Jan 1 - pricing questions

Evelyn —

We’ve been reviewing our upcoming renewal and expansion needs. Usage is up Q3 over last year and the team wants clarity on two items before we lock dates: (1) whether you can preserve current per-token rates until June (price-hold) if we agree to a modest uplift in committed capacity; (2) how credits would be applied if we overrun the commit in a quarter.

Leah and I are available next week for a quick sync — can your team put together a proposal with numbers (discount, credits, soft cap triggers)?

Thanks,
Sanjeev
Head of ML Platforms
Centrica

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning for Jan 1 - pricing questions

Sanjeev — thanks for the note and the context. I’ve pulled Ben and Marissa in to help with a concrete term sheet. High level thoughts: we can offer a price-hold through 2027-06-30 if Centrica moves to a stepped commit (quarterly bands) with a 15% uplift across committed tokens this year and a modest one-off credit to cover Q1 ramp.

I’ll attach a short term sheet and a usage breakdown for Q3 so you can see how the proposal maps to your actual consumption. Can we do a 30 minute call on Thursday to walk through and capture any procurement constraints?

Best,
Evelyn
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Centrica-Renewal-Termsheet-v1.pdf; usage-breakdown-q3.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev@centrica.io>, Leah Kim <leah.kim@centrica.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning for Jan 1 - pricing questions

Quick note on mechanics that came up with Finance: the price-hold requires a minimum committed baseline (we were thinking 15% uplift) but we can define a soft cap for monthly overages — above the soft cap we apply a blended overage credit instead of immediate overrate. That gives Centrica predictability for spikes while protecting unit economics. I put two example band tables in the term sheet: band A (up to 110% baseline) — no additional charge; band B (110–140%) — blended credit of 40% of the overage delta; band C (>140%) — overage at standard overrate.

This structure is intended to avoid a hard shock for seasonal spikes while creating a clear incentive to increase commit if usage stays high.

Ben
Senior Account Executive

From: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev@centrica.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Kim <leah.kim@centrica.io>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning for Jan 1 - pricing questions

Thanks Evelyn & Ben — this looks promising. A couple of clarifying items from procurement: 1) can the band thresholds be measured on a rolling 90-day basis (not calendar quarter)? 2) the blended credit sounds reasonable but we need a cap on total quarterly credits (procurement asks for an annual cap so our finance team can model worst-case). 3) can you confirm whether the one-off ramp credit is refundable if we cancel mid-year?

We can take Thursday’s slot; Leah and I will bring our procurement lead.

—Sanjeev

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev@centrica.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Leah Kim <leah.kim@centrica.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning for Jan 1 - pricing questions

Sanjeev — great questions. Short answers below and we’ll cover in the call: 

1) Measurement window: yes, we can use a rolling 90-day lookback for band calculations. We’ll include language that the system evaluates trailing 90-day consumption at each billing date.

2) Credit cap: Redwood can set an annual credit cap equal to 12% of the committed spend under the stepped-commit structure. If Centrica needs a different number, we can flex but that will adjust the price-hold concession.

3) Ramp credit refundability: the one-off onboarding/ramp credit is *non-refundable* if Centrica terminates early — it is intended to offset our operational onboarding and committed capacity reservation. We can offer prorated reinstatement of credits towards future purchases if you shift the start date within 60 days.

Call details: Thu 2026-11-19 10:00 AM GMT (join link in calendar invite). I’ve asked Marissa to prepare an alternate termsheet with a slightly higher annual cap (16%) and a second option that uses a smaller uplift (10%) but a longer price-hold (through 2027-09-30).

Thanks — talk soon.
Evelyn
